top_stories.title: Demis Hassabis steps down as Google DeepMind CEO, becomes Alphabet chief scientist
points: Hassabis leaves the day-to-day DeepMind CEO role to become Alphabet's chairman and chief scientist, focusing on AGI (artificial general intelligence — AI that matches or beats human ability across any task), which he believes is now within reach.
Koray Kavukcuoglu, a 13-year DeepMind veteran and CTO, becomes senior vice president reporting directly to Sundar Pichai, overseeing Gemini, Frontier AI research, and the Gemini app.
Gemini now has roughly 950 million monthly users, making the handover one of the biggest leadership changes in Google's AI org.
The move is part of a broader Google AI reshuffle happening alongside Jeff Dean's departure.

unique_angles.point: Hassabis will spend more time at Isomorphic Labs, Alphabet's drug-discovery arm that uses AlphaFold (an AI that predicted 200 million protein structures) to target diseases like cancer.
Notes Hassabis specifically inherits the chief scientist title vacated by Jeff Dean.

top_stories.title: Meta launches Muse Code, its first AI coding agent
points: Muse Code is a terminal-based coding agent that plans changes, writes code, and validates results across entire repositories via a single-command install, now in preview.
It splits large codebase changes across persistent parallel sub-agents so work is coordinated automatically instead of manually.
Pricing is pay-as-you-go with a contributor tier reportedly 10+ times cheaper than rivals like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.
Built under Alexandr Wang at Meta Superintelligence Labs, it is Zuckerberg's attempt to monetize massive data center and compute spending.

unique_angles.point: The underlying Muse Spark 1.2 model is now available via API.

items.title: Jeff Dean leaves Google after 27 years to found Discovery Loop
points: Dean, Google's chief scientist, departs with three other top researchers: Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals.
Discovery Loop will be a public benefit corporation building self-improving AI that advances with minimal human intervention.
Google will invest, collaborate, and guarantee compute resources for at least one year, signaling an amicable split.

items.title: Cloudflare OS: open-source operating system for AI productivity
points: Agent-based chat interface where every file is a custom AI-generated application built to the user's spec, developed in a sandbox (isolated environment that limits what code can touch).
A security framework applies guardrails (behavioral restrictions) to both agents and generated apps to prevent misuse.
Released fully open source so companies can customize and deploy it internally.

items.title: Conduit builds thought-to-text 'telepathy' for AI
points: Founded by a former OpenAI researcher, it trains models on non-invasive neural data (brain signals read from outside the skull, no surgery) to turn thoughts into text.
Scaling requires far more data collection plus specialized hardware to read neural signals.
Goal is AI as a direct extension of human cognition rather than a separate tool.

items.title: SpaceX to attempt mid-air Starship catch on Flight 14
points: The flight, targeted before end of August, would catch Starship's upper stage out of the sky for the first time.
Same mission also deploys Starlink V3 satellites.

items.title: Prime Intellect's Prime Agent beats Claude Code and Codex on long-range coding
points: Claims 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3, outperforming Claude Code and Codex on long-horizon tasks.

Uses parallel sub-agents spun out from a central harness, converting repeated fixes into reusable skills to avoid context rot (performance decay when an AI's working memory fills with old or irrelevant information).
Designed for indefinite sessions without quality decay.

items.title: Cerebras case study: internal knowledge base handling 15,000 questions a day
points: Pulls data from 6+ platforms (Slack, GitHub, Jira, Google Docs) into a single searchable Postgres table; hit 15,000 daily queries after three months.
An LLM auto-generates a clean record per Slack thread (question, summary, fix, systems mentioned) since engineers phrase the same problem differently.
Code is embedded semantically (converted to numeric vectors capturing meaning) rather than keyword-grepped, and only changed code is re-embedded on each commit.

items.title: Figure AI's Handoff agent automates websites without APIs
points: Claims parity with GPT 5.4 and Opus 4.8 while completing web tasks end-to-end by clicking and typing on live sites like Walmart and LinkedIn.
Opens automation for services that expose no public API (a programmatic interface other software can call).

items.title: DeepSeek V4 runs inside Codex for 90%+ cost savings
points: Heavy users can cut AI coding costs by over 90% versus standard proprietary API pricing.

items.title: Builder tools and resources
points: Meta Ray-Ban glasses tutorial covers designing apps for 600x600 displays, gesture controls, and pairing-code security.
A token wastage calculator shows where coding agents burn tokens, enabling leaner context windows (how much prior conversation a model can consider at once).
A Codex-based repo mapping tool generates clickable HTML maps of module dependencies, callers, and test coverage, flagging changed modules on re-run.
62 LeetCode-style interview problems tailored to AI/ML engineer hiring rounds.

items.title: AI coding incidents and community backlash
points: A developer reported Claude Code wiped a user folder instead of backing it up, replying with just two words — a warning about agents with full filesystem access.
Growing fatigue over AI-generated feedback in code reviews and Slack, with devs coining new terms to flag low-effort AI suggestions.

items.title: Apple's iCloud Private Relay can leak real IP addresses
points: Three WebKit features bypass proxy settings and expose real IPs: WebAuthn Related Origin Requests (since iOS 18), DNS prefetching, and WebTransport (both added in iOS 26).
The WebAuthn leak needs no user prompt to trigger; proxy-based browsers Psylo and Onion Browser are affected too.
Apple told 404 Media it is investigating with a fix planned for fall 2026, and many sites may already have harvested leaked IPs.

items.title: OpenAI moves to dismiss Apple's trade secrets lawsuit
points: OpenAI says it has 'no use, need or desire' for Apple's confidential tech and that Apple's July complaint names no specific trade secret or proof anything was taken.
The suit targets OpenAI and two former Apple employees, centering on AI hardware; analysts expect OpenAI to build a phone-like device.
The two companies remain partners, with ChatGPT accessible via Siri and subscriptions available in iOS settings.

items.title: Google's Ask Maps chatbot can now order food
points: Conversational food ordering arrives via Toast and Square partnerships.
Also adds hotel booking and event discovery tied to Gmail integration.

sections.title: 1. Prime Intellect Raises the Bar on AI Coding
points: Prime Agent claims 95.5% accuracy on ARC-AGI-3 benchmarks, exceeding Claude Code and existing Codex implementations on long-range tasks.

Designed for indefinite sessions without performance decay, addressing a core limitation of traditional coding agents that struggle with project scope over time.

sections.title: 2. Building Enterprise Knowledge Bases (Cerebras Case Study)
points: Cerebras pulled company data from 6+ platforms (Slack, GitHub, Jira, Google Docs, etc.) into a single Postgres table with unified search interface, handling 15,000 daily queries.

For each Slack thread, an LLM auto-generates clean records (question, summary, fix, systems mentioned) to capture meaning beyond keyword search, since engineers describe the same problem different ways.
Code repositories get embedded semantically rather than grepped by keywords, catching code that keyword-only search misses; re-embedding only changed code on each commit to stay current.

sections.title: 3. New Coding Agents Expand Automation Boundaries
points: Meta's Muse Code splits large codebase changes across persistent parallel sub-agents, allowing it to plan, execute, and validate across entire repositories without manual coordination.

Figure AI's Handoff agent automates web tasks by clicking and typing through live sites (Walmart, LinkedIn), enabling automation on services that lack APIs—a capability previously impossible for coding tools.
DeepSeek V4 models integrated into Codex provide 90%+ cost savings for heavy users versus direct API pricing, adding a low-cost alternative to proprietary coding models.

sections.title: 4. Practical Resources for Builders
points: Meta Ray-Ban glasses tutorial covers designing apps for 600x600 resolution displays with gesture controls and pairing code security for AI glasses development.

Token wastage calculator helps teams track unnecessary AI spending by showing exactly where coding agents consume data, enabling prompt optimization and leaner context windows (the amount of prior conversation an AI model can consider when generating responses).
Codex-based repository mapping tool creates clickable HTML maps showing module dependencies, callers, and test coverage, automatically flagging changed modules on each re-run.

sections.title: 5. AI Coding Incidents and Community Trends
